title: Complex diagnostics of the corrosion of heat exchangers

segments.text: The thermogalvanic and heat-transfer corrosion of carbon steel and copper in hydrocarbonate and chloride media were studied with experimental models simulating operation conditions of heat exchange equipment.

Being capable of significantly (from 2 to 7 times) increasing the total losses and either intensifying or mitigating the local damage, these kinds of corrosion must be taken into account when complexly diagnosing the corrosion of heat transferring surfaces.

title: The thermal diffusion of hydrogen chloride in aqueous solutions of acetonitrile

segments.text: The results obtained in measurements of the initial and stationary temperature voltage coefficients of symmetrical thermogalvanic elements with silver-chloride and quinhydron electrodes in the HCl-H2O-CH3CN system at 298.15 K were used to determine the Soret coefficients and standard entropies of thermal diffusion transfer of hydrogen chloride and the entropies of the H+ and Cl- ions moving in solution.
The results obtained are discussed using the De Bethune thermal diffusion model and the Agar theory.

title: Electrochemical determination of standard thermal diffusion characteristics for chlorides of hydrogen and potassium in water-ethanol solutions

segments.text: Initial and steady-state temperature coefficients of the voltage generated by thermogalvanic cells comprising silver chloride and quinhydrone electrodes in the systems HCl-H2O-C2H5OH and KCI-H2O-CH5OH are determined.
Standard thermal diffusion Soret coefficients, the entropy of thermal diffusion transport of electrolytes, and the entropy of mobile ions H+, K+, and Cl- are calculated for 298 K.
The effect the nature of ions and the solvent composition exert on the obtained thermal diffusion transport characteristics is considered in terms of the De Bethune theory.

title: High performance eutectogel-based thermocell with a wide operating temperature range through a water-containing deep eutectic solvent strategy

segments.text: Flexible ionic thermoelectric (i-TE) quasi-solid cells provide an electrolyte leak free, easy-operation and mechanically adaptable route to low-grade heat harvest.
However, limited by freezing and evaporation, the hydrogel-based thermocell exhibits environmental instability and has difficulty functioning at low temperatures.
Herein, we develop a high-performance cryo-temperature i-TE eutectogel using a water-containing deep eutectic solvent (DES) strategy.
The water containing DES is intentionally utilized to modulate the solvent shell structure of redox couple and expand the operation temperature range of i-TE eutectogel cell.
Moreover, appropriate amount of water can increase the solubility of [Fe(CN)6]3-/4- , while maintaining the eutectic properties of DES.
Subsequently, a double-network polymer gel is constructed to prevent liquid electrolyte leakage and provide the flexibility and operability of the i-TE cell.
After synergistic optimization of the solvent and the polymer network, the Seebeck coefficient of the fabricated i-TE eutectogel cell reaches 2.06 mV/K.
In a 20-cell prototype module, the current and voltage at Delta T = 8.3 K are 0.033 mA and 0.33 V, respectively.
The DES endows this cell wide operable temperature ranging from-60 degrees C to 80 degrees C.
The anti-freezing capability of this eutectogel cell offer a new strategy for fabricating gel-based thermocell required in frigid regions.
